cards.text: While Apollos, another preacher, is over in Corinth, Paul the apostle travels through the interior and comes to Ephesus. That's a long walk, friend, and I get winded hopping from one oven to the next. When Paul gets there, he finds some disciples.
No 'nice weather,' no 'love the sandals.' Paul skips the small talk and asks them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?”

cards.question: When Paul asks about the Holy Spirit, these disciples tell him they've never even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.

cards.text: I bet Paul's thinking what I think when a batch comes out flat: something's missing from this recipe. So he asks, “Into what, then, were you baptized?”

cards.question: What baptism do these disciples in Ephesus tell Paul they received?

cards.text: Paul explains that John's baptism was a baptism of repentance, and John told people to believe in the One coming after him. John was pointing the whole time, friend, and not at himself.

cards.question: According to Paul, who is the One coming after John that John told people to believe in?
On hearing what Paul explains, the disciples in Ephesus are baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

cards.text: Then Paul lays his hands on them. And friend, this is where it gets GOOD.

cards.question: When Paul lays his hands on these disciples, what happens?

answers.text: The Holy Spirit comes on them and they speak in tongues and prophesy
A bright light flashes around them and they all fall to the ground
The whole building shakes and every door in the place flies open

cards.question: Counting the disciples Paul met in Ephesus, there were about ___ men in all.

cards.text: Then Paul goes into the synagogue and speaks boldly, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God. Bold AND persuasive, friend, when I can't even persuade my oven timer to wait two more minutes.

cards.question: Paul keeps speaking boldly in the synagogue in Ephesus for three ___.

cards.text: But some of them stubbornly refuse to believe and publicly malign the Way. That's leaving a one-star review while you're still standing at the counter.

cards.question: With some in the synagogue publicly maligning the Way, what does Paul do?

answers.text: Takes his disciples to the lecture hall of Tyrannus
Sails out of Ephesus and heads back to Syria
Stays and argues in that same synagogue every day

cards.question: Paul's daily discussions go on for two ___, so that everyone in the province of ___ hears the word of the Lord.

cards.text: Now God does extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul. Not ordinary, friend, EXTRAordinary.

cards.question: God's miracles through Paul are so extraordinary that even ___ and ___ that had touched him are taken to the sick.
When the things that had touched Paul are taken to the sick, the diseases leave them, but the evil spirits stay.

cards.text: APRONS, friend, and the most mine has ever done is catch flour. Meanwhile, some traveling Jewish exorcists try to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over people with evil spirits.

cards.question: Over people with evil spirits, these traveling exorcists command them by Jesus, whom ___ proclaims.

cards.text: Notice that, friend: it's Jesus, whom PAUL proclaims. And among the ones doing this are the sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest.

cards.question: The exorcists using Jesus' name include ___ sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest.

cards.text: Then one day they try it, and the evil spirit answers back. Friend, when the thing you're commanding starts talking back, that is NEVER a good sign.

cards.question: What does the evil spirit tell the sons of Sceva?

answers.text: It knows Jesus and knows about Paul but asks who they are
It will only leave if Paul comes himself
It has never heard the name of Jesus

cards.text: Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even THERE nobody hit me with “who are you?” Then the man with the evil spirit jumps on them.

cards.question: When the man with the evil spirit jumps on the sons of Sceva, he overpowers all of them.
The attack is so violent that the sons of Sceva leave the house how?

answers.text: They run out naked and wounded
They are carried out in chains
They are led out blind by the hand

cards.text: Word gets to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear comes over all of them. Friend, seven men running out of a house like that does not need a group chat.

cards.question: With fear over everyone in Ephesus, whose name is held in high honor?

cards.text: Then many who had believed come forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds. Friend, that's the kind of honesty that makes a whole kitchen go quiet.

cards.question: In Ephesus, what do a number of those who had practiced magic arts do with their books?

answers.text: Burn them in front of everyone

cards.question: When the value of the burned books is calculated, the total comes to fifty thousand ___.
After all this in Ephesus, the word of the Lord powerfully continues to spread and prevail.

cards.text: Ephesus is buzzing, friend, and Paul's journey is just getting warmed up. Keep that oven on, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: About 9 of the 20 choice cards can't be reasoned out from earlier cards. They are pure recall of details the baker hasn't seen: the baptism of John (S1 C5), twelve men (S1 C11), three months (S1 C13), the hall of Tyrannus (S1 C15), two years and Asia (S1 C16), handkerchiefs and aprons (S2 C2), seven sons (S2 C7), naked and wounded (S2 C12) and drachmas (S2 C17). That is far more than a few. Several of these need more setup on the story card before them, or should become different questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The exact head count of about twelve men neither moves the passage forward nor helps the baker understand it. It is trivia, and it can't be reasoned out. It would fit better told on a story card.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: This asks for the currency unit (drachmas), which is trivia the baker can only guess. What matters in the moment is how huge the value was, and that could be told on a story card instead.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The two blanks can be swapped. A baker who puts 'aprons' in blank 1 and 'handkerchiefs' in blank 2 is just as faithful to the meaning, but would be marked as missing it. The two blanks need distinct, non-interchangeable slots, or the card should use a single blank.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer (13 words) is noticeably longer and more detailed than the wrong answers (9 and 7 words), so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The line 'Not ordinary, friend, EXTRAordinary' reads as mild wordplay, not a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The line 'that's the kind of honesty that makes a whole kitchen go quiet' is pleasant but not funny. A moment of mass confession could hold a real laugh, for example self-deprecation about something Papa Dorin would have to confess himself.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The line 'this is where it gets GOOD' is a plain hype line with no joke. It reads as a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The final card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from Acts 19:20, which was already asked on card 18. Even so, it cites Acts 19:20.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its verses field cite: the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else?
